turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): tess? in you come. shoes off on the scales, obs first, then the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): yep. make it quick, yeah? bub's in the pram and i'm just about done.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): scales say fifty-two kilograms. last time in March you were sixty-eight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): sixty-eight was pregnant and puffy. fifty-two seems light, but i'm not fighting your scale.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): i'll record fifty-two. blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): one-forty was in labour. i was scared out of my wits, course it was up.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): temperature thirty-eight point three. pulse is ninety-six... err, wrong line. pulse is eighty-six. oxygen's ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): i don't feel hot. it's just stuffy in here.
[SEG0009] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): chart says ferrogradumet three hundred and twenty-five milligrams every morning. still taking that?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): no. chemist swapped it. bottle says two hundred milligrams. i take two— no, one. one in the morning.
[SEG0011] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): right, i won't guess the dose. doctor reeves will want the bottle. have a seat.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): hi tess, i'm doctor reeves. sorry to run late. your partner's pacing out there, he looks quite anxious. joining us?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): dan can stay out. he hovers, i get snappy, then i feel like rubbish.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): alright. what brought you in?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): i can't sleep. even when the bub sleeps i'm awake. she's six weeks and i cry at nothing.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): when did the not-sleeping start?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): ugh, the car park, twenty minutes circling, maisie screaming, i nearly just—
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): sorry. not from the birth. maybe three weeks, maybe a fortnight, and it's every night. i can't pin the start.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): so roughly a fortnight to three weeks, not from day one. how does a night go?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): i feed her, she settles, i'm still awake with my brain chewing on everything. round four i'm crying in the kitchen.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): every night?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): every night. and i'm foul in the day. went at dan over the dishwasher, then felt sick about it.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): the mood underneath that?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): flat. tired even when i'm sitting. nothing's fun. i know i love her but i don't feel it properly. sounds rotten.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): it sounds like a hard six weeks, not rotten. appetite?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): off. toast, if that. i'm breastfeeding so i ought to eat, and i can't be bothered.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): any breast pain, redness, flu-type aches?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): no. bit full in the morning, that's the milk. not sore, no redness, no aches.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): stinging when you pass urine, or going more often?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): no. that's fine.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): chest or breathing?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): no. both normal.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): and bowels?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): slow since the pregnancy. not new. doesn't hurt.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): i have to ask straight. any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): no. i want sleep, not an exit.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): any thoughts of harming maisie?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): no. never. don't write it like i'm unsure.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): you said no. that's the note. anxious spells, or not wanting to be alone with her?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): anxious, yeah. not panic. i can be alone with her. dan's the anxious one, keeps checking i'm safe. does my head in.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): any thyroid trouble, asthma, depression before the baby? any allergies?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): no, none of that, and no allergies. my mum had postnatal depression after my brother. she told me in the car park like it was my turn.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): operations?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): no. vaginal birth, small tear, no stitches. no operations ever.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): smoking, alcohol, work?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): never smoked. no grog while i'm feeding. high school teacher, on maternity leave. dan lives with us and he's off this week.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): thinking out loud, this is postnatal depression until proven otherwise. not sleeping when she sleeps, tearful, flat, the bond feeling thin. i can't rule out iron or the thyroid adding to the tiredness, and thirty-eight point three means i also can't drop infection off the list, even with no pain.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): i really don't feel feverish. i already said.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): heard. we'll let the tests talk. bloods today, full blood count, ferritin and a thyroid test, plus a urine sample while you're here. starting sertraline, fifty milligrams, by mouth, once every morning, for the mood. it's used in breastfeeding.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): will that knock me out? i can't be foggy with her.

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): sleep can be a bit worse for a few days, then mood usually picks up. not a sedative. if thoughts of harm turn up, emergency department or the mental health line, same day, don't wait. and let dan take one night feed with expressed milk so you get a stretch.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): he's desperate to. i've said no. that might be me being stubborn.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): i'm referring you to the perinatal mental health team, they'll make contact. i want to see you in two weeks. bring the iron bottle and we'll settle two hundred versus three twenty-five. keep taking one each morning until then. reception will book the bloods and the appointment, and dan's welcome next time.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): two weeks. yeah. okay. sorry i came in cranky.

spec.situation: Mother six weeks after delivery, tearful, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps; partner present and anxious; denies harming herself or the baby when asked directly; support and follow-up planned.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
